subject: chemistry
title: Oxidation numbers and redox agents
key_idea: An **oxidation number** shows how oxidised or reduced an atom is. **Oxidation** is a loss of electrons and an increase in oxidation number. **Reduction** is a gain of electrons and a decrease in oxidation number. An oxidising agent is reduced, and a reducing agent is oxidised.

blocks.text: Redox reactions are reactions where oxidation and reduction happen together. This section covers the definitions.

items.meaning: Loss of electrons, or an increase in oxidation number. It can also be gain of oxygen.
Gain of electrons, or a decrease in oxidation number. It can also be loss of oxygen.
A reaction in which one substance is oxidised and another is reduced.
A substance that oxidises another substance and is itself reduced.
A substance that reduces another substance and is itself oxidised.

items: An **oxidising agent** gives oxygen to another substance, or takes electrons from it.
A **reducing agent** takes oxygen from another substance, or gives electrons to it.

blocks.label: Equation
where: Al gains oxygen, so it is oxidised and is the reducing agent.
Fe₂O₃ loses oxygen, so it is reduced and is the oxidising agent.

blocks.label: Ionic equation
where: Zn loses two electrons, so it is oxidised.

items: Zinc is the reducing agent.
Silver ions are the oxidising agent.
Oxidation is loss of electrons. Reduction is gain of electrons.
An oxidising agent is reduced. A reducing agent is oxidised.
A redox reaction has oxidation and reduction at the same time.

blocks.text: An oxidation number is a number given to an atom to track electrons. This section covers the rules and how to use them.

items: An atom in an uncombined element has an oxidation number of **0**.
A monatomic ion has an oxidation number equal to its charge, such as +2 for Mg²⁺.
The oxidation numbers in a compound add up to **0**.
The oxidation numbers in an ion add up to the **charge** on the ion.
Oxygen is –2 and hydrogen is +1 in most compounds. Chlorine in chlorides is –1.

items.text: In SO₄²⁻, each O is –2. There are four O atoms.

items.lead: Set the total to the charge.

items: A Roman numeral in a name gives the oxidation number of the element before it.
Manganese(IV) oxide contains manganese with an oxidation number of +4.
Chlorine(I) oxide contains chlorine with an oxidation number of +1.
Iron(III) oxide contains iron with an oxidation number of +3.

items: An element on its own is 0. An ion's numbers add up to its charge.
A Roman numeral gives the oxidation number.
Reaction with oxygen increases an oxidation number: that is oxidation.

blocks.text: You can find redox reactions and agents by looking for changes in oxidation number. This section covers the method and two colour tests.

items.lead: Write the oxidation number of each element.
items.text: Do this on both sides of the equation.
Look for an element that goes up and one that goes down.
The substance that contains the element that goes down is the oxidising agent. The substance that contains the element that goes up is the reducing agent.

items: In 2Mg(NO₃)₂ → 2MgO + 4NO₂ + O₂, nitrogen goes from +5 to +4. It is reduced.
In Fe₂O₃ → Fe, iron goes from +3 to 0. It is reduced.
In 4NH₃ → 4NO, nitrogen goes from –3 to +2. It is oxidised.
(Supplement) **Acidified potassium manganate(VII)** is purple. It is an oxidising agent. It turns **colourless** when it is reduced by a reducing agent.
(Supplement) **Aqueous potassium iodide** is colourless. An oxidising agent oxidises iodide ions to iodine, and the solution turns **brown**.

items: A rise in oxidation number is oxidation. A fall is reduction.
Purple manganate(VII) turning colourless shows a reducing agent.
Potassium iodide turning brown shows an oxidising agent.

worked_example.question: The reaction of sulfur chloride S₂Cl₂ with chlorine is a redox reaction. S₂Cl₂(g) + Cl₂(g) ⇌ 2SCl₂(g). The oxidation number of Cl in S₂Cl₂ and in SCl₂ is –1. Use oxidation numbers to explain why: sulfur is oxidised in the forward reaction, and chlorine is oxidised in the reverse reaction.
answer_points: The oxidation number of S goes from +1.
The oxidation number of S goes to +2.
The oxidation number of Cl goes from –1 to 0 (in Cl₂).
The oxidation numbers of Cl and S both increase, so both are oxidised.
worked_example.tip: Give the numbers each time, not just the words 'increase' or 'decrease'.

worked_example.question: This is the ionic equation for the reaction between zinc and silver nitrate solution. Zn(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s). Explain, in terms of electrons, why this is a redox reaction.
answer_points: Zinc is oxidised because it loses electrons.
Silver ions are reduced because they gain electrons.
worked_example.tip: Say what happens to the electrons, and name which substance does it.
